title: StreamMixer must close its BytesIOCopy streams before the shared output buffer

note.title: StreamMixer must close its BytesIOCopy streams before the shared output buffer
answers: intermittent error at teardown when using CliRunner from multiple threads
I/O on closed file flaky in typer/click tests with threads
note.body:
Symptom: tests that use CliRunner (for example through typer) from multiple threads fail very rarely (about 1 in 10k runs) with an error during stream cleanup or garbage collection.
Root cause: src/click/testing.py:StreamMixer holds `stdout` and `stderr` as BytesIOCopy objects that write into the shared `self.output`. When GC finalized them in arbitrary order, `output` could be closed first, and then a later stream flushing on close wrote into the closed buffer (related to cpython#136248).
Fix pattern: StreamMixer.__del__ closes the streams in a fixed order: stderr, then stdout, then output. Any copy-to stream must be closed before the buffer it copies into.
Constraints: if you add another BytesIOCopy (or any stream with copy_to=self.output) to StreamMixer, close it in __del__ before `self.output.close()`. This is a separate bug from click#824 (issuecomment-3027263262); this patch does not fix that reproducer. The race is nondeterministic, and no test reproduces it reliably.
note.applies: src/click/testing.py StreamMixer and any stream that copies into a shared buffer
